## Submitting to the chart {#getting-your-dot-on-the-chart-route-2}

You submit twice, and the two are different in kind. The browser lab and the workspace use the same function names.

**Task 4 – the exploratory dot (green).** Nothing in this task is preregistered.

1. **`try_spec(...)`** – one argument per decision, every one defaulting to the specification you reproduced. `try_spec(estimator = "fe_country")` changes one thing and leaves the rest alone. An option that left the curve, such as `estimator = "pooled_cl"`, stops with the reason and the page that teaches it.
2. **`my_experiments()`** – prints everything you have tried so far, side by side, with only the decisions that varied.
3. **`submit_exploration()`** – sends the most recent try to the chart, labelled as exploration. Open the printed link and press **Send**. It also prints your tag, such as `amber-otter-42`, which marks your submissions on the class chart; `submit_exploration(nickname = "...")` sets your own instead.

**Task 5 – the declared dot (black).** Here you preregister one specification before you run it.

4. **Preregister.** Make one choice for every decision in the preregistration cell (`claim_align <- TRUE` is already set for you), then run `prereg()`. The completed cell is your preregistration. In the workspace, run the cell before you write the model code of step 5, and keep it in the report as set out under [Rendering the report](#rendering-your-report-route-1); on the browser lab page, copy the whole cell into your notes.
5. **`build_model(...)`** – write your specification as a formula. It accepts only code that matches your preregistration and tells you what is off when it does not.
6. **`run_spec(my_model)`** – computes your specification and shows the coefficient, its claim-aligned partial *r* (below zero supports the claim), its p-values under CR2 and the wild cluster bootstrap, its class, and its placement among the 864 specifications on the curve.
7. **`report_result()`** – no arguments needed. It builds your submission from the preregistration and prints a clickable, pre-filled form link; open it and press **Send**. It reuses your tag from Task 4. In the browser lab, if you have reloaded the page since then, pass the tag back with `report_result(nickname = "your-tag")`.

If any of that stalls, work down the list below.

---

## A stalled browser lab

The browser lab runs R inside your browser tab, and browsers occasionally baulk. Work down this list. Each step is more certain than the one before, and step 4 puts your dot on the chart whatever your machine does.

1. **Hard reload, then rerun.** Reload the page clearing the cache (Ctrl+Shift+R / Cmd+Shift+R), wait for R to restart, and **rerun the chunks above** the one that failed – webR needs the earlier chunks to have run in this session before a later one will work.
2. **Switch browser.** If a chunk still will not run, open the browser lab in a different browser (Chrome, Edge, or Firefox). A fresh browser clears most stubborn webR problems.
3. **Follow the shared screen – the 'buddy chunk'.** If your machine simply will not cooperate, watch the facilitator run the same chunk on the shared screen and read the printed results from there. You miss no step by doing this.
4. **Read your printed result to the facilitator.** If `submit_exploration()` or `report_result()` printed your result but the form link will not open, read the printed `b`, `se`, `t`, `df` and claim-aligned `r` to the facilitator, who adds the dot to the chart for you (every specification on the curve uses all 270 country-years, so `n` is 270). The lab has already applied the claim-alignment convention, so there is nothing to convert, and no working form link is needed at your end. If a cell refuses to run at all, nothing is printed and there are no numbers to read, so give the facilitator your fourteen choices instead, and the facilitator reads the result off the curve file by hand (the note below).

::: {.callout-note}
## The by-hand lookup
Last resort, facilitator-side, if a participant's cells will not run at all: every specification on the curve is one row of `data/spec_curve.csv`, picked by its thirteen axis codes (`outcome`, `predictor`, `copredictor`, `estimator`, `sample`, `weights`, `construction`, `noop`, `item_set`, `cell_weight`, `measure`, `pred_form`, `family`), and the reproduced specification is the row in which `is_reference` is TRUE. The inference rule is not part of the lookup, because every row carries all of its p-values and the class of every point is read from the bootstrap (`p_wcr`). Read off `b`, `se`, `t`, `df` and `n_cells`, and take `r` from the `r_ca` column, which is already claim-aligned. Then apply to `b` and `t` the one flip that the lab applies automatically, reversing their sign for a GDP-growth predictor. Enter those into the [form]({{< var results-form-url >}}), and the dot appears without anything being fitted.
:::

## IDE quick fixes

| If ... | Then ... |
|---|---|
| A package will not load, or `feols` is "not found" | Run the checker again – `source("R/check_setup.R")` – and run the install line that it prints; or install by hand, e.g. `install.packages("fixest")`. |
| The `pak` install that `R/check_setup.R` prints stalls or half-finishes | Restart R (Session menu), then run the install again; a second pass usually completes what the first left. |
| "Permission denied" while installing a package | Let R use a personal library it can write to – accept the offer from R to create a personal library, then reinstall. |
| A data file is "not found" | Check you opened the unzipped **folder** in your IDE (File → Open Folder in Positron and VS Code; the `.Rproj` file in RStudio), not a single file – the paths in the code are relative to that folder. |
| Something not listed here | The [setup help page](../help.qmd) has the longer table, with links to the discussions where each problem was solved, and prompts to give an AI assistant. |
| Everything is stuck | Open the [browser lab](browser-lab.qmd) and carry on there. You lose nothing required. |

## Rendering the report {#rendering-your-report-route-1}

Render your report once your preregistration block is complete. The rendered copy carries the date on which it was rendered and keeps the declaration above the cells that fit the specification. In Positron and in RStudio, press the **Render** button at the top of the open report. In VS Code, run the Render command of the Quarto extension. In any of the three you can also run `quarto render index.qmd` in a terminal. On the browser lab page the same block is a cell on the page, and it updates in the tab when you run it.
